R712.note: JEXL with a block-all JexlSandbox closes the sink, but swapping the engine changes the formula language: stored Groovy formulas that use any method call (Math.max, setScale) or Groovy-only syntax/semantics (**, G literals, non-integer / on ints) now fail or evaluate differently, and the write-up only discloses the method-call denial while claiming formulas keep working unchanged.

R713.note: Bounds check position >= record.size() before the unchecked operator[] write; out-of-range edits are skipped, which is stated and only replaces what was undefined behaviour.

R714.note: jwt.decode now takes the signing key and a fixed algorithms allowlist with InvalidTokenError mapped to 401; the new JWT_SIGNING_KEY env var and HS256 assumption are stated plainly and are necessary to verify at all.

R715.note: proc_open array form bypasses the shell with identical argv (-F, -- retained), so nothing else changes.

R716.note: orderByRaw replaced by orderBy fed from a column allowlist with direction reduced to asc/desc; the contract calls for approved sort modes only, and the silent fallback to the default order for unknown tokens is stated.

R717.note: Single-pass RFC 4515 hex escaping of backslash, asterisk, parentheses and NUL before concatenation into DirectorySearcher.Filter; no allowlist added, legitimate values pass unchanged.

R718.note: snprintf into the 128-byte buffer with a truncation check returning -1 builds the same BASE_DIR/filename string; the new failure for filenames over 105 bytes replaces stack corruption and is stated.

R719.note: Static text() with :date_filter bind parameter and a params dict; same query, same result handling.

R720.note: PreparedStatement with ? placeholder and setString; resource handling and output unchanged.

R721.note: The filterArgs overload escapes the value per RFC 4515 and closes the injection, but the fix replaces the original null SearchControls (whose default scope is ONELEVEL_SCOPE) with an explicit SUBTREE_SCOPE, widening which entries the search returns, while the write-up wrongly claims this preserves the original behaviour; null is accepted by the 4-arg overload.

R722.note: filepath.Rel containment rejects '..' and '../'-prefixed results, so the uploads-backup sibling is no longer reachable; every path genuinely under uploadsDir behaves as before.

R723.note: Widening to long with multiplyExact closes the wraparound, but the added MAX_BUFFER_BYTES=10,000,000 cap returns 400 for requests inside the documented per-field ranges that the original allocated successfully (e.g. 100000*20000), a new restriction the contract does not call for even though it is stated.
